subject: treasureChest
pitch: A pirate's treasure chest with its lid thrown open. Weathered dark wood planks bound with rusty iron straps and studs, a heavy padlock hanging loose, and spilling out of it: gold coins, a pearl necklace, a jewelled goblet and a few red and green gems. A small skull-and-crossbones is carved on the front.
reasoning:
I'm planning the chest model's dimensions and proportions—roughly 0.9m wide, 0.55m deep, 0.5m tall body with a hinged lid opening at the back around 110°, positioned standing on the ground plane. I'm sketching out how to build it from box primitives using the SDK.

Now I'm working through how joints and poses should work: the lid needs a hinge joint at the back top edge, and I'm figuring out whether to build its parts in the closed position and then rotate via pose, since parts attached to a bone move with that bone's joint when posed.

Working through the trigonometry, I confirm that rotating the lid joint by -110° about the X axis correctly swings the lid open and backward so its tip lifts up and tilts back. For the chest contents, I'm planning to keep coins, necklaces, goblets, and gems placed directly inside and spilling over the body's rim rather than attaching them to the lid.

I'm thinking through part budgets: coins as flattened cylinders can stay as individual parts since ~60 is well within limits, pearls can be strung as spheres along a curved path using a frame-based placement helper, and the goblet can be built with a lathe profile. For the gems I'll use faceted octahedron or icosahedron geometry, and for the skull-and-crossbones decoration I'll build a simple cranium sphere with small eye sockets and crossed rotated box or capsule shapes rather than anything more detailed. I'm also planning iron straps as boxes placed at intervals across the front planks.

Now I'm working out the padlock and chest body construction: a box body with a torus shackle hanging loosely from the hasp, and wood texture achieved by applying a grain paint pattern with dark brown tones along one axis. For the chest itself, I'm laying out box dimensions for the body and planning to build it as separate wall panels — front, back, sides, and floor — so the interior reads as hollow with a slightly recessed floor for contents to sit above.

For the inside, I'm placing a gold coin heap using a squashed sphere scaled down in height so it mounds up near the rim, letting some spill over for a natural look. For the lid, I'm figuring out hinge placement at the back top edge and positioning the lid box relative to that hinge so it sits closed on top of the chest, and considering whether to add a curved half-cylinder on top for a domed shape, though the rotation and orientation math for that is getting complicated.

I'm sorting out whether coordinates for lid parts attached to a bone should be given in model space or relative to the bone, deciding based on the API pattern that `at` is meant as model-space coordinates even when a bone is specified, so I can just use the closed-pose position and let the bone handle posing afterward.

I'll call pose once at the very end, after all lid geometry (including straps and studs) is built on the lid bone, so everything rides along together rather than trying to build the open pose directly. For the padlock, I'm deciding where the hasp sits now that the lid is open, likely placing it lower on the front of the body rather than on the lid itself, and letting the lock hang loose from it.

I'm positioning the padlock on the front of the chest, with a small box for the body and a torus with an open arc for the shackle to suggest it's unlocked and dangling, roughly placed to the side so it doesn't collide with the skull-and-crossbones carving I'm also placing on the front panel.

Now I'm detailing the skull using a sphere and jaw box with small dark eye sockets, plus two crossed rods beneath it to form the bones, and then shifting to iron reinforcement straps wrapped around the body as thin boxes with studs at intervals.

For the chest's contents, I'm planning gold coin cylinders scattered randomly inside and spilling onto the floor near the front, using rotation for tilt variation across about 65 parts, followed by a pearl necklace built along a curved path draped over the coin pile and spilling past the rim.

Now I'm designing a goblet sitting atop the coins, built as a lathe shape with a profile outline that forms the base, stem, and cup walls -- working out the outer and inner wall points so the rim and interior read as a hollow vessel without the profile self-intersecting.

I'll place the goblet upright on top of the gold pile, tipping slightly into the pile's surface so it looks nestled in the coins, with gems scattered using red and green octahedron shapes. For the wood, I'll use a grain-paint texture with horizontal streaks to mimic plank boards on the chest body, considering whether to add subtle groove lines between boards for extra realism.

Now I'm defining the interior structure: a dark wood floor box, four wall segments sized to overlap at the seams, and a lid built as a single hinged box at the back with a trim band. I'm calculating hinge rotation math to figure out how far open the lid should swing (around -105 to -110 degrees about the X axis) so its tip ends up pointing up and back realistically.

I'm working out positions for iron corner bands, studs, a skull-and-crossbones carving on the front panel, and a loosely-hanging padlock with a torus shackle, adjusting heights so none of these decorative elements overlap awkwardly. I'm also setting up coin-scattering logic with randomized positions and tilts for the pile inside the chest and the spilled coins in front, plus placing the goblet sinking slightly into the gold pile near the edge.
